You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

"
     * Calculates the Cholesky decomposition of the given matrix.
     * @param matrix the matrix to decompose
     * @param relativeSymmetryThreshold threshold above which off-diagonal
     * elements are considered too different and matrix not symmetric
     * @param absolutePositivityThreshold threshold below which diagonal
     * elements are considered null and matrix not positive definite
     * @exception NonSquareMatrixException if matrix is not square
     * @exception NotSymmetricMatrixException if matrix is not symmetric
     * @exception NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException if the matrix is not
     * strictly positive definite
     * @see #CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix)
     * @see #DEFAULT_RELATIVE_SYMMETRY_THRESHOLD
     * @see #DEFAULT_ABSOLUTE_POSITIVITY_THRESHOLD
     "

Diagnosis:

The test case testMath274 expects a NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException to be thrown when attempting Cholesky decomposition on a given matrix. The matrix is:

{  0.40434286, -0.09376327, 0.30328980, 0.04909388 },
{-0.09376327,  0.10400408, 0.07137959, 0.04762857 },
{ 0.30328980,  0.07137959, 0.30458776, 0.04882449 },
{ 0.04909388,  0.04762857, 0.04882449, 0.07543265 }

The test expects this matrix to not be positive definite, thus the exception.

Looking into CholeskyDecompositionImpl constructor, this constructor calls another constructor with default thresholds for relativeSymmetryThreshold and absolutePositivityThreshold. In the main constructor:

- It first verifies the matrix is square.
- Then checks each diagonal element of the matrix against absolutePositivityThreshold, throwing NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException if any diagonal element is below this threshold.
- Then it checks the symmetry of the matrix off-diagonal elements, throwing NotSymmetricMatrixException if matrix is not symmetric enough.
- Then sets lower triangle of the matrix to zero as preparation.
- Then it performs the Cholesky decomposition algorithm.

The key here is the check at lines 114-115 for diagonal elements against absolutePositivityThreshold. If the test matrix has diagonal elements all above this threshold, no exception will be thrown at this step.

Note also the test matrix's off-diagonal elements in the first row are negative. The Cholesky method checks for symmetric off-diagonal with a threshold of relativeSymmetryThreshold. The test matrix is symmetric with respect to signs, so no symmetry exception is expected.

The current bug report says the matrix with positive off-diagonal elements works fine (no exception), but changing one entry from positive to negative causes the test to fail (exception), indicating possible sensitivity of the code to sign or threshold values.

A likely issue is that the default thresholds used in CholeskyDecompositionImpl constructor are not suitable for this matrix to detect it as not positive definite. Possibly the original matrix is positive definite but the test matrix's minor changes (sign change) should cause exception but did not because of the thresholds allowing it to pass the diagonal positivity test or symmetry test.

Hence, the bug is that the CholeskyDecompositionImpl does not correctly identify the matrix as not positive definite for this test case, likely due to the thresholds it uses internally when checking diagonal positivity and symmetry.

The recent bug reports do not seem very relevant and do not discuss Cholesky decomposition or matrix positivity checks.

In conclusion, the root cause is in the constructor CholeskyDecompositionImpl(RealMatrix) which calls the main constructor with default threshold parameters that may be too lenient for this matrix causing the decomposition not to throw NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException as expected.

Suggested locations to fix or investigate would be CholeskyDecompositionImpl constructor and the threshold values used for the test transition from positive definite to not positive definite. Possibly the test should specify tighter thresholds or the code should be revised to detect non-positive-definiteness more robustly.

This explains why the test is failing when it expects an exception but no exception is thrown.

Summary:

- The test expects NotPositiveDefiniteMatrixException.
- The code checks for positivity via threshold on diagonal elements.
- The default threshold might be too lenient.
- Matrix with sign-changed elements still passes diagonal check.
- Exception not thrown as expected.
- Need to improve or adjust threshold handling in CholeskyDecompositionImpl constructor.

This matches the reported issue of testing for symmetric positive definite matrix and failing to raise exception correctly.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
